recipes.name: "If Looks Could Kale" Burger inspired by Bob's Burgers
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed + drained
1 cup short grain brown rice, cooked
For the “If Looks Could Kale” Burger
1 bunch curly kale, washed + dried + stems removed
1 1/2 lb Ground Beef or Veggie Burger Mix (see recipe above)
As needed freshly ground black pepper
instructions: For the Ground Beef
Place the grinding attachment tools in the freezer to chill for at least 30 minutes before using.
Cut each of the beef cuts into about 1-inch cubes. Transfer them to a parchment-lined sheet tray(s) and freeze for 20 minutes. - ⅔ lb roast chuck - ⅓ lb brisket trimmed - ⅓ lb boneless short ribs
Grind the meat through the medium grind attachment, alternating cuts of beef.
Keep refrigerated until ready to cook, up to 2 days.
For the Veggie Burger Mix
Preheat a large skillet with neutral oil. - 1 tbsp neutral oil
Add the chard stems and onion to the skillet, cook for 4-6 minutes or until the vegetables are tender. - 1 cup chard stems chopped - ⅓ cup yellow onion chopped
Add the garlic to the pan and cook for an additional minute. - 1 garlic clove minced
Transfer the cooked vegetable mixture to a rimmed baking sheet. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature.

Combine the black beans, cooled vegetable mixture, and miso in the bowl of a food processor. Process the mixture until well combined but still chunky. - 1 can (15 oz) black beans rinsed + drained - 1 tbsp red miso

Transfer the bean mixture to a large bowl and fold in the brown rice, egg white, seasonings, and breadcrumbs. - 1 cup short grain brown rice cooked - 1 egg white - 1 tbsp nutritional yeast - 1 tsp kosher salt - ½ tsp smoked paprika - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper - ¼ tsp cumin - ⅛ tsp cayenne - ¼ cup breadcrumbs
Refrigerate the mixture for at least 30 minutes before shaping or up to 4 days.
For the “If Looks Could Kale” Burger
Preheat the oven to 375 °F.
Tear the kale into 2-3 inch pieces, then transfer them to a parchment-lined baking sheet. - 1 bunch curly kale washed + dried + stems removed

Drizzle the kale with the olive oil, garlic powder, and kosher salt. Toss to combine, then bake the kale for 15-25 minutes or until completely crisp. - 3 ½ tbsp olive oil - ½ tsp garlic powder - As needed kosher salt

Meanwhile, season the beef with salt and pepper, then divide the beef into 4 equal portions. Shape them into patties about ½ inch larger than the diameter of the burger buns. If using the Veggie Burger Mix, shape the mixture into 4 equal patties the exact size of the hamburger buns. Freeze the veggie patties for 30 minutes before cooking. - 1 ½ lb Ground Beef or Veggie Burger Mix (see recipe above) - As needed freshly ground black pepper - As needed kosher salt
Preheat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat with neutral oil. - 1 tbsp neutral oil
Cook the burgers on each side for 4-5 minutes or until cooked to your desired doneness.
Turn off the heat and place a slice of cheese over each burger. Cover the skillet with a large lid for 2-3 minutes or until the cheese is melted. - 4 slices gruyere cheese
Assemble the burgers by placing each burger on one half of the buns, top with the cooked kale chips and the bun top. - 4 hamburger buns toasted
Serve immediately.
